cards.text: Judah's king Jehoiakim has died, and his son Jehoiachin takes his place in Jerusalem. His mother is Nehushta, daughter of Elnathan, from right there in Jerusalem. And the new king is just eighteen years old, friend, with a whole kingdom on his shoulders.

cards.question: Eighteen-year-old Jehoiachin becomes king of Judah. He reigns in Jerusalem for three ___.
King Jehoiachin turns things around and does right in the sight of the LORD.

cards.text: Three months on the throne isn't a reign, friend, it's a FREE TRIAL. And at that time, the servants of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, march up to Jerusalem.

cards.question: The servants of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, have marched up to Jerusalem. What happens to the city?

answers.text: It sends out its army to fight

cards.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar comes to the city himself, while his servants are still besieging it. You know it's serious when the boss stops sending emails and shows up at your desk with his coat still on.

cards.question: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, is at Jerusalem himself. What does King Jehoiachin do?

answers.text: He surrenders to the king of Babylon
He sneaks out of the city at night
He rides out to fight the king of Babylon

cards.question: Jehoiachin surrenders to the king of Babylon all by himself, while his mother and his officials stay out of it.

cards.text: So the king of Babylon takes Jehoiachin captive. Then Nebuchadnezzar turns his eyes to the house of the LORD and the royal palace.

cards.question: At the house of the LORD and the royal palace, Nebuchadnezzar leaves the treasures right where they are.
Long ago, Solomon, king of Israel, made gold articles in the temple of the LORD. What does Nebuchadnezzar do with them?

answers.text: He leaves them in the temple
He hands them to his servants

cards.question: Nebuchadnezzar carrying off the treasures of the LORD's house and the palace happens just as the LORD had declared.

cards.text: Then he carries all Jerusalem into exile: the commanders, the mighty men of valor, the craftsmen and the metalsmiths. That's TEN THOUSAND captives in all.

cards.question: The commanders, the mighty men, the craftsmen and the metalsmiths are all taken from Jerusalem. Who stays behind in the land?

cards.text: Jehoiachin goes to Babylon too, with his mother, his wives, his officials and the leading men of the land. The king of Babylon also takes seven thousand men of valor and a thousand craftsmen and metalsmiths.

cards.question: The seven thousand men of valor and the thousand craftsmen and metalsmiths taken to Babylon are all strong and fit for ___.
With Jehoiachin gone, the king of Babylon makes Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's ___, king in his place.

cards.text: Then the king of Babylon changes Mattaniah's name to Zedekiah. When I got my fresh start, the ONE thing I asked for was to keep my name, so believe me, I'd be holding that name tag with both ends of my mustache.
And that's where we'll set this batch down for now, friend. Judah's got a brand new king with a brand new name, and trust me, this story is not done yet.

findings.problem: Verse 9 says Jehoiachin did evil 'just as his father had done,' but no card ever tells this. Card 3 only asks whether he did right, and the answer is False, so the baker never learns he followed in his father's steps. Also, 'turns things around' assumes things were already bad, which no earlier card has said.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question says the servants 'have marched up to Jerusalem,' which rules out the wrong answer 'They march right past it.' That leaves only two real choices.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: No earlier card hints that the LORD had spoken about the temple treasures, so the baker can only guess. Cards 2, 3, 11, 12, 14 and 17 are all discovery questions, about half the choice cards. That is more than 'a few.'

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Card 19 retells what card 18 already told ('a brand new king with a brand new name') and adds nothing new from the passage. Verse 17 was already asked on card 17, so this card can be just the line saying the story isn't over, or that line can be added to the end of card 18.

Several story cards are plain retellings with none of Papa Dorin's voice: card 1, card 9, card 13 (only the capital letters) and card 15. Only cards 4, 6 and 18 try for a laugh. A siege, the temple gold cut into pieces and ten thousand captives leave room for his reactions and disbelief without changing any facts.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
